g.text: 1. Hull: carvel outside planking over an inner double-diagonal skin, 12 frames, rock elm timbers.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 2. Sheer: 0.908 m above LWL at the stem head, 0.773 m at the transom; sheer strake is painted white.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 3. Machinery is carried on two wrought-iron longitudinal bearers bolted to the floors (see D-002).

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 4. The canopy is a canvas hood on brass hoops carried by the coaming; the funnel passes through it.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 5. Boiler: vertical fire-tube, 0.720 m dia x 0.860 m, ~110 psi working; coal bunker abaft the boiler.

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: 6. Proportion of this boat follows the 1888 Admiralty *proposed* 25 ft steam cutter (RMG NPC9572);

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4a4a

g.text: equipment is reconstructed, not documented - see HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE.md.
